targets.authors: Solon, M, Park, H. I., Dehghan-Chaleshtori, M., Carver, C., & Long, A. Y.
targets.title: Exploring an elicited imitation task as a measure of heritage language proficiency.
targets.evidence_quote: This study is a partial replication of Solon, Park, Dehghan-Chaleshtori, Carver & Long (2022), who administered an EIT originally developed for advanced L2 learners on a group of HSs.
targets.outcome_quote: Solon et al.’s (2022) Wright map presented a very similar distribution, and the 36-item EIT showed that the EIT mapped better with the HSs’ ability than the 30-item version. Their ability covered 9.49 logits and the item difficulty covered 7.06 logits. The present study showed similar proportions, though seemingly less discriminating across the entire sample: Learners’ ability covered 10 logits and item difficulty 6 logits.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly compare the Rasch distributions to the target and report very similar distributions and proportions. Somewhat reduced discrimination does not overturn the supported finding. The instrument remains effective for most participants.

reasoning: A new sample tests the published validity and discrimination finding in Solon et al. (2022). The 2019 instrument-development work supplies materials; 2023 rater findings and other proficiency studies are background rather than additional targets. Novel concurrent-validity comparisons extend the target.
